text:
sam: FYI - spotted another period of extreme GPU imbalance in us-west last night. 10/12 GPUs showing ~95% idle while two GPUs had 100% queues and jobs stuck for minutes.
maya: ugh. any obvious correlates? deploys, autoscaler spikes?
devon: saw a burst of long seq requests (~6-8k tokens) from a single customer route around 02:17 UTC. admission queue jumped.
sam: attaching the small log snippet I grabbed from the scheduler pod:
```
[2025-11-02T02:17:03Z] admit: route=gen-long seq_len=7100 customer=acme priority=standard gpu_pool=west-1
[2025-11-02T02:17:03Z] enqueue->pool(west-1): queue_len=3 inflight_per_gpu=0
[2025-11-02T02:17:03Z] dispatch: picked node=west-1-a gpu=0
[2025-11-02T02:17:03Z] admit: route=small-chat seq_len=48 customer=prod-b priority=low gpu_pool=west-1
[2025-11-02T02:17:04Z] enqueue->pool(west-1): queue_len=4 inflight_per_gpu=1
[2025-11-02T02:17:04Z] dispatch: picked node=west-1-a gpu=0
[2025-11-02T02:17:05Z] dispatch: gpu=0 saturated, holding queue head - nothing scheduled on gpu=1..11
```
maya: looks like the scheduler keeps picking gpu=0 for both long and short jobs -> head-of-line blocking on that GPU lane.
elaine: could be the placement score function favoring GPUs with certain topology or cache warmness. last rollout changed the kernel-selection scoring.
devon: I reproduced locally. If you send a long request then follow with many small requests, the small ones stick behind because we only have a single FIFO per pool, not per-gpu lanes.
sam: that matches metrics: per-pool queue length spikes, but overall GPU utilization aggregate is low because only a couple of GPUs carry the load.
infra-bot: alert: [fleet] west-1 pool imbalance detected - imbalance_score=0.88 - pg: scheduler
maya: temporary mitigation: we can tweak admission config to enable per-gpu slotting and lower max_inflight_per_gpu. Proposed change:
```
admission:
  per_gpu_queues: true
  max_inflight_per_gpu: 4  # was 8
  admit_window_ms: 50
```
sam: we should be careful lowering max_inflight - might increase latency for long requests. but per_gpu_queues should avoid starving small ones.
devon: also found a bug in the scoring comparator: when cache_affinity_score tie, comparator returns 0 instead of using gpu_id as tiebreaker, leaving selection non-deterministic -> bias toward first node in list. I'll open a patch.
elaine: can you paste failing comparator snippet?
devon: here:
```
// comparator: returns -1,0,1
if (a.cache_affinity == b.cache_affinity) return 0; // <-- bug: should break ties by available_slots
return a.cache_affinity > b.cache_affinity ? -1 : 1;
```
maya: nice catch. that would let the first gpu in the pool get chosen repeatedly when scores equal.
sam: action items:
- devon: open PR to fix comparator + add unit test for tie-break (ETA 6h)
- maya: stage config change with per_gpu_queues=false->true + lower max_inflight in canary (ETA 2h)
- elaine: run canary load with mixed seq lengths and validate 95th latency for small routes (ETA 4h)
- infra-bot: create incident if imbalance_score > 0.7 after canary rollout

devon: opening PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/482
maya: starting canary now on west-1-a subset, will watch queue_len and per-gpu utilization.
sam: thanks. if we see improvement, plan a full rollout with a short maintenance window.
elaine: one more thought - maybe set a tiny preemption window for short tasks so they can cut in front of long-running low-priority ones. that's more complexity but might help customer-perf.
maya: agree but prefer first to fix deterministic selection + per-gpu queues. preemption as follow-up.
sam: agreed. ping us on this thread with perf graphs. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2025-112 - west-1 queue imbalance (owner: oncall)
